rationale: The student counted the starting number as the first count ('12, 11, 10') instead of counting the hops/transitions backward (12 -> 11 is 1 hop, 11 -> 10 is 2 hops, 10 -> 9 is 3 hops). A number line subtraction demonstration modeling hops back helps correct counting the numbers rather than the hops.

script.focus: each backward hop from 14 to see that 3 hops lands on 11, not counting 14 as the first hop

intent: Demonstrate subtract on the number-line with values [14,3]. Tutor points at: each backward hop from 14 to see that 3 hops lands on 11, not counting 14 as the first hop

content.title: Counting back, one hop at a time

frames.caption: Start at 14. We are standing here; we have not hopped yet.
Hop 1 moves one back and lands on 13. The first number we count is where we land, not where we started.

judgement.reasoning: The demonstration explicitly addresses the student's exact misconception ('We are standing here; we have not hopped yet' and 'The first number we count is where we land, not where we started'). It uses a passive worked demo on a fresh problem (14 - 3 instead of 12 - 3) to lower the cognitive load.
judgement.verdict: Yes, this demo directly targets counting the starting number by explicitly highlighting that standing still is not a hop.
